text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says Jerusalem bombing is "linked to what preceded it by events and massacres committed to obstruct the peace process".
- Proposals drafted to restructure Agriculture Ministry.
- King Hussein, referring to Moslem Brotherhood's boycott of November parliamentary elections, says "only dialogue that is desired is the one which is in the interests of the nation".
- Six left-wing opposition parties decide to take part conditionally in parliamentary elections if government gives guarantees on fairness and freezes tougher press law recently enacted.

- Arab Bank resumes leadership of stock market; share gets close to breaching 300-dinar ($423) psychological level on prospects of improved half-year earnings and imminent move to lift 50 percent ceiling on foreign ownership.

- Suicide bombers return with their response to Israeli extremism; king says Jerusalem bombing is closely linked to massacre committed by Jewish settler Goldstein (of worshippers in Hebron) and assassination of Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.
- Jordan comes number two in amounts of Japanese aid provided to region.
- King tells army cadets at graduation he hopes his countrymen will bring to parliament capable deputies.
